Uriah the Hittite
yoo-RYE-ah
proper noun
Hebrew Uriyyah, “the LORD is my light,” a Hittite by birth and one of David’s faithful soldiers, the husband of Bathsheba.

Biblical Definition

Uriah the Hittite was one of David’s mighty men, a faithful soldier and the husband of Bathsheba, whom David wronged in the darkest deed of his reign. When David had sinned with Bathsheba and sought to hide it, he called Uriah home from the war, that he might go down to his house; but Uriah, in his soldierly integrity, refused, saying, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house? as thou livest, I will not do this thing (2Sa 11:11). Unable to cover his sin by Uriah’s faithfulness, David wrote to Joab to set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle and retire from him, that he might be smitten and die (2Sa 11:15); and so the loyal soldier was slain. But the eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good (Pro 15:3), and the prophet Nathan laid the murder bare: thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword (2Sa 12:9). The dictionary marks Uriah as the faithful man wronged by the great, whose integrity shines the brighter against the king’s sin, and whose innocent blood was not hidden from God, but avenged in the chastening of David’s house.

Webster 1828 Definition

A faithful soldier of David, husband of Bathsheba, murdered by the king’s plot to hide his sin.

URIAH THE HITTITE, a faithful soldier of David and husband of Bathsheba.

David sinned with his wife and sought to hide it.

Uriah refused to go down to his house while the army was in the field.

David had him set in the forefront of the battle to be slain.

His innocent blood was avenged in the chastening of David’s house.

Key Scripture

2Sa 11:11 — "And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing."

2Sa 11:15 — "And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die."

2Sa 12:9 — "Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon."

Pro 15:3 — "The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good."

Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; the faithful man wronged by the great, whose innocent blood God did not hide but avenged.

expand to see more

Uriah has drawn no redefinition from the present age, surviving as the faithful soldier slain by David’s plot. The dictionary records him that the reader may mark the integrity that shines the brighter against the king’s great sin.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the eyes of the LORD are in every place, and the innocent blood of the wronged is not hidden from Him. David, the man after God’s own heart, fell into murder to cover adultery; but Nathan laid it bare, thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and the chastening fell heavy on David’s house. Uriah’s soldierly faithfulness is honoured, and his innocent blood avenged; and the great are warned that no power or place can hide a wrong from the God who beholds the evil and the good, and who will surely require the blood of the faithful at the hand of the mighty.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the LORD is my light,” Uriah names the faithful soldier wronged and slain by David.

expand to see more

Uriah — Hebrew Uriyyah, “the LORD is my light.”

He was a Hittite by birth and one of David’s mighty men.

He was the husband of Bathsheba.

He refused to go home while the army was in the field.

He was slain by David’s plot, and his blood avenged.

Usage

"Like Uriah, the faithful man wronged by the great is not forgotten by God."

"The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good."

"No power can hide a wrong from the God who avenges innocent blood."
